Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options — follow up and constraints

Thanks Evelyn — quick summary from our side: BrightCart needs a predictable SLA commitment for our checkout pipelines (p95 latency < 150ms) and an uptime guarantee tied to monthly credits. Procurement will only accept a maximum 10% annual uplift on our current spend for a 24-month term. Also critical: we require a documented escalation path that includes an on-call rotation for P0 incidents and a named escalation engineer within 2 hours.

Can you share a compact proposal that maps commit tiers to credits, a sample escalation RACI, and any qualifying requirements for the reduced pricing tier (e.g., commit volumes, traffic shaping, or tooling integration)? We need this for our procurement review next week.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, BrightCart
elena@brightcart.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options — compact proposal (first pass)

Elena — thanks for the clarity. I spoke with Product and Pricing and put together a short first-pass that maps three commitment tiers to uptime bands, response windows, and named escalation support. Summary below (full proposal attached):

- Tier A (Baseline, no commit): 99.5% uptime, P1 response 8h business, P0 on-call via shared queue; no credits
- Tier B (Committed 12–24 months): 99.9% uptime, P1 response 4h, P0 named escalation with 2h acknowledgement; 5% usage credit on monthly invoice if uptime falls below target
- Tier C (High-commit): 99.95% uptime, 24/7 P0 on-call with 1h named escalation acknowledgement, incident bridge facilitation; 10% usage credit slab and custom runbook integration

Qualifying for Tier B/C: 6-month rolling commit of token/embedding volume (we provide a forecast template), integration of our tracing hooks (lightweight) so we can diagnose cross-service issues faster, and a readiness checklist (attestation on internal runbooks).

Attached: SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf (compact tables) and a pricing-breakdown-commit-scenarios.xlsx with modeled discounts.

Next steps I propose: 1) Elena + Procurement review the attachment; 2) Marissa and Ben to cost-validate and sign off on guardrails; 3) if acceptable, we draft a 1-page amendment for procurement and start a 30-day pilot for Tier B.

Thoughts?

— Evelyn

Subject: Re: SLA options — internal cost and escalation notes

Looping in my quick notes after reviewing the attachments:

- Pricing: Tier B with a 12–24 month commit and the 5% usage credit is doable if BrightCart commits to a 30% uplift vs their current monthly baseline (we'll need the forecast to model). Tier C needs at least a 50% uplift or a material platform integration premium, because 99.95% requires reserved capacity on Dedicated pools for critical windows.
- Escalation: We can provide a named escalation engineer for Tier B but limit it to business hours for the first 3 months unless they accept the Tier C premium. For P0 handling we should define SLA acknowledgement (2 hours) and bridge facilitation (we join within 30 minutes after acknowledgement).
- Operational guardrails: require a weekly health report during pilot, and a runbook attachment to the contract that we can update with change control.

Recommended negotiation posture to present to procurement: start with Tier C terms but offer Tier B pricing if they sign a 24-month commit and accept the tracing hooks and runbook attestation. That gives a path to Tier C in 90 days based on observed traffic and reliability.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Pricing | Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Marissa — thanks, this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. A couple of final asks before we can greenlight the pilot:

1) Can you tighten Tier B's P0 acknowledgement window to 90 minutes for the pilot? Our risk committee will accept a shorter acknowledgement if it's time-boxed to the pilot period only.
2) For credits, procurement wants the credit to be applied as a contiguous monthly usage credit (not an annual true-up).
3) We need the named escalation engineer's role (and backup) to be included in the MSA amendment language.

If you can accept (1) and (2) and provide draft MSA language for (3) we can route to procurement this afternoon and aim to start the 30-day pilot next Monday.

I'll attach procurement's redline if we proceed.
